subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should canonical `openai` auto session route state be owned by the OpenAI provider doctor contract, the Codex doctor contract, or a generic auto-fallback doctor repair?
rationale: The defect is source-proved, but the durable ownership boundary affects provider/plugin contracts and future upgrade behavior.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical route repair
options.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract or equivalent owner for literal `openai` auto session route/auth state while leaving Codex to own legacy Codex ids.

options.title: Codex claims openai
options.body: Extend the Codex doctor owner to include literal `openai`, accepting that Codex owns cleanup for canonical OpenAI agent-route state.

options.title: Make auto repair generic
options.body: Move auto-sourced stale override cleanup out of provider ownership when current route evidence proves the override stale.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical route repair
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract or equivalent owner for literal `openai` auto session route/auth state while leaving Codex to own legacy Codex ids.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the two closest merged doctor/Codex route-state repairs and are the strongest history match for the owner-boundary decision.
